key_insight: Adapting language models to patients’ diagnosis histories and combining multiple model experts improved 180-day opioid overdose risk prediction over general-purpose baselines.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help flag higher-risk patients earlier using routine EHR diagnosis data, potentially supporting more targeted prevention workflows.
method: Continued pretraining on one year of longitudinal ICD diagnosis sequences
Task-specific fine-tuning for 180-day opioid overdose risk prediction
Multi-expert ensemble (OVERDOSEMOE) combining different model scales with complementary weighting strategies
evidence_signal: On the study cohort, OODQWEN reached AUPRC 24.47 and AUROC 68.56, while OVERDOSEMOE improved to AUPRC 25.17 and AUROC 69.49; results also generalized to an independent MIMIC-IV cohort.
watch_item: Performance was tested on retrospective EHR data, so real-world utility depends on prospective validation, calibration, and careful integration into clinical workflows.
paper_title: OverdoseMoE: A Multi-Expert Framework for Opioid Overdose Risk Prediction
